$comment: Single source of truth for what ships and to which agents. The render step reads this; nothing is rendered unless listed here. scope: universal = rendered into AGENTS.md prose + every target; claude = .claude/ only (uses Skill tool / subagents / hooks); codex = .codex/ only.

rules.$comment: Rules are always universal; they are plain principles. Languages limited to the working set observed in usage (go, python, typescript, rust).

rule_overrides.$comment: Per-file scope overrides. A rule file marked 'claude' ships to targets/claude/rules but is excluded from the universal AGENTS.md, for content that is genuinely a Claude Code mechanism, not a portable principle.

agents.$comment: Claude subagents map to Codex .codex/agents/*.toml where a clean equivalent exists; the rest are claude-only. Reviewers/architect/explorer translate; build-resolvers are claude-only (tightly tool-coupled).

skills.$comment: Formula-invoked working set. 'claude' ones lean on the Skill/subagent mechanism; 'universal' degrade to AGENTS.md prose so Codex and Amp still get the practice.

workflows.$comment: Ported formula step-DAGs. Universal ones render as AGENTS.md workflow sections, .claude/commands, and .codex/prompts. fleet-conformance is claude-only: it drives a specific installed scanner binary with no portable equivalent, so it ships to .claude/commands only.

templates.$comment: Project-scaffolding templates, NOT principle prose: they ship verbatim into every target's templates/ dir (and are excluded from the AGENTS.md universal layer). The init flow / install.sh instantiates them into a consuming project. AGENTS.project.md is the thin pointer-style project AGENTS.md; COMPASS.md is the per-area tribal-knowledge map.
